column1: # Tajikistan (`tj.default`, class D (none): Calculated by Taqwa; Generic.kt's tajikistanRegion and tajikistanAt, spec
# §6.2 c). REAL rows: Tajikistan's 31 app cities are routed to tj.default, and the tables held for the country are the
# Islamic Centre's Council of Ulama's own (shuroiulamo.tj, its official site; the engine survey of 11 Nov 2026: the
# Islamic Centre is the only official Islamic body and mosques are state-registered, so majority use is inferred, not
# surveyed). Gated first by the safe defaults lane (12 Nov 2026) on one month; the trust audit's F16 (13 Nov 2026) found
# that proof to be one in-sample month with no spare, and this file is what answered it.
# What is held, all of it at Dushanbe as the Council prints it:
# - its month page of November 2026 (shuroiulamo.tj/tj/namaz, 30 days; archive/raw/manual/tj-council/2026-11-11/, parsed
#   by archive/code/manual/tj-council/council_month.py): the starts of Bomdod (F, also the end of eating: no sehri column
#   is printed, the stricter reading, as ru-dumrd.tsv), Peshin, Asr (the Hanafi Asr as printed), Shom and Khufton, and
#   Bomdod's end as the sunrise (an end);
# - its nine Ramadan calendars of 2018 to 2026 (nine posts of its own news list, plain GETs of 13 Nov 2026;
#   one an image transcribed by hand): Subhi sodiq (F, also the end of eating), the sunrise (S, an end; not printed in
#   2024 and 2026) and Shom (M). Between them the nine editions cover 19 Feb to 15 Jun.
# The towns: the month page and seven of the nine calendars print a footnote of each town's minutes before or after
# Dushanbe, on every time. Two sets are in print, an older (2020 to 2023, 2025) and a newer (2024, 2026, the month
# page), up to 4 min apart for the same town; 2018 and 2019 print none. Every town of every footnote is a row of its
# own, a DERIVED table (Dushanbe's + that edition's printed minutes, as the Council defines them): 19 places, nine of
# them at the app's own point and nine (Rasht, Asht, Murghob, Hamadoni, Sh. Shohin, Muminobod, Shahritus, Ayni,
# N. Khusrav) not app cities, at the district centre's point as the lane knows it (approximate: Generic.kt holds them
# with a 30 km band, N. Khusrav 60).
# What a DERIVED row proves: that the engine holds the Council's printed rule for the town (Dushanbe's day moved by the
# footnote's minutes) and that the town's own sun never comes on the wrong side of it. It is not a table the Council
# printed for the town, and the engine reproduces it by construction.
# So of the 124 rows below, 10 are REAL (Dushanbe's own: the month page and the nine calendars) and 114 are DERIVED town
# rows, 50 of them at the nine approximate points.
# Three cells are READINGS, not the print (the lane's reviews, 14 Nov 2026). The Council misprints the hour of the Shom
# of 27 May 2019 (printed an hour after the days on either side, its minute between theirs; read an hour earlier) and
# of the Bomdod of 26 and 27 Feb 2026 (printed an hour before the days on either side, their minutes between theirs;
# read an hour later): the minutes fit the column, so the hour is put right
# and the reading BINDS as a printed cell would (it was left out of the tables at first, and a day nobody checks is a
# day an early start could hide on). Each table's own header names its readings; the 2026 ones run through its 17
# Found on tj.default as the safe defaults lane left it (one start point per town from the month page's footnote, sunrise
# 2 min before the sun's, the end of eating at Fajr − 10, Maghrib + 13, Isha Maghrib + 90), against all 124 rows:
# - Asr 1 min before the printed Asr on 7 place-days, Maghrib 1 min before the printed Shom on 7 and Isha 1 min before
#   the printed Khufton on 5: 17 of the 19 at Asht in November 2026 (a town of the footnote the app does not list, so a
#   user there took a neighbour's lower figure), 2 in the 2020 edition (Bokhtar and Shahritus, a day each);
# - Maghrib with no spare (+ 0) on 64 place-days;
# - the sunrise shown after the printed one (a late end) on 465 place-days in 26 rows, up to 8 min (Khorugh's 2021); at
#   Dushanbe itself on 32 of 239 days (the 2021 edition 19 days up to 5 min, 2019 7, 2018 4, 2025 2);
# - the end of eating after the printed Subhi sodiq (a late end) on 511 place-days in 29 rows, up to 8 min
#   (Istaravshan's 2025); at Dushanbe on all 29 days of the 2025 edition, up to 5 min.
# The fix (ruling R207, Generic.kt): every town of both footnote sets is held, listed by the app or not; a place takes
# the latest minutes any town it may be nearest to prints for its starts and the earliest for its ends (a start point and
# an end point at Dushanbe's latitude moved by them, as ci.default's), over its own sun; the sunrise is 12 min before
# the sun's own (sunriseMinutes − 9, the 2021 edition's worst and a spare); the end of eating is the 19.5° dawn, never
# Fajr less a fixed span (the 2025 edition's worst and a spare); Isha is the later of the 18° dusk + 2 and Maghrib + 90
# (Khufton is Shom + 90 on every day held, and nothing is held for summer); Dhuhr is never before 12:45 anywhere in
# the country. After it: 0 early, 0 late ends; every start at least 3 min after the printed one but Dhuhr, held by the
# 12:45 floor, and every sunrise at least 2 min before the printed one.
# What it cost, against the printed rule (the late limits in Generic.tajikistanLateLimits): Fajr up to 31 min after
# Bomdod (Isfara, Ramadan 2025; Dushanbe 26: the 15° Fajr against a dawn near 18°), the sunrise up to 21 before
# (Ayni, 2020; Dushanbe 17), Dhuhr more than 20 after a town's own Peshin (Murghob; Khorugh more than 10), Asr 11, Maghrib 15
# (Khujand, Isfara, Asht; Dushanbe 10), Isha 10, the end of eating up to 34 before Bomdod (Asht, 2020; Dushanbe 30).
# Nothing is held out, and the stamp says so: the margins above were read off these very tables (the Dhuhr floor,
# Shom after sunset and Khufton after Shom off November; the sunrise off the 2021 edition; the end of eating off the
# 2025 one; the town figures off both footnote sets), so every row is a fit row, the nine Dushanbe calendars included.
# So this file is proof that the build holds the tables it was made from, and no proof of a table nobody has seen:
# every one of its Ramadan place-days is a day of a PAST Ramadan (2018 to 2026) the margins were read off. Which
# edition binds which margin: the sunrise's − 9 rests on 2021's alone (the others print the sunrise 0 to 9 min before the
# sun's own), Maghrib's + 13 on the June days of 2018 alone (2026 prints the sunset + 7 to 8.5), the end of eating on
# 2025's, the 15° Fajr on none (it is Central Asia's latest, up to 31 min after the Bomdod held).
# What is not held: any day from 16 Jun to 31 Oct or from 1 Dec to 18 Feb; Peshin, Asr and Khufton outside November
# (the month page shows the other months only through a form the lane does not send). Ramadan 1448 begins about 8 Feb
# 2027, so its first eleven days or so fall where NO edition held prints a day (the earliest day of any is 19 Feb):
# there the app's times rest on the margins above and on the sun, not on a printed day. Whether Peshin stays at one minute all
# year and Khufton Shom + 90 in summer is not known: the 18° dusk and the 12:45 floor are the safe side of both. The
# first table nobody has seen is December's page, on or after 1 Dec 2026; then the Ramadan 1448 calendar.
